text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- Exports fell 19.26 percent to $646 million in January from $800 million in December and imports rose 6.18 percent to $1,019 million from $960 million.
- The consumer price index rose 2.17 percent in January and the wholesale price index 2.30 percent.
- The caretaker government has recovered $116 million in unpaid bank loans and utilities bills from politicians.
- Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto's residence near her home town of Larkana was raided by police last night and one of her servants was arrested.

- The Pakistan People's Party has filed four petitions before the Election Commission in Islamabad about alleged irregularities in the February 3 general elections in four constituencies of the Sindh provincial assembly.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- China is willing to acquire high technology from Pakistan for its textile sector to produce fine quality yarn.

- Japanese and South Korean investors have indicated that Pakistan will turn into a safe haven for investment, comparable to Sri Lanka and Indonesia, in the Nawaz Sharif government, said Iqbal Mangrani, former chairman of Yarn Merchants Association.
FINANCIAL POST
- Pakistan has received $95 million as remittances from overseas Pakistanis on the appeal of Nawaz Sharif.
- Eight British multinational companies have complained to the government that problems hampering their business operations in Pakistan remain unresolved.
THE NEWS
- Sardar Mehtab Abbasi has been tipped as the new chief minister in North West Frontier Province.
- Caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid wants Nawaz Sharif's government to continue the accountability process in Pakistan.
- Benazir Bhutto hopes her party will be able to form the provincial government of Sindh.
THE NATION
- Shahbaz Sharif, younger brother of Nawaz Sharif, is likely to be the new chief minister of Punjab.
- Nawaz Sharif met the Chief of the Army Staff General Jehangir Karamat and discussed security matters.
- The voter turn-out in February 3 general elections was 35.92 percent, provisional data released by Election Commission said.
